messages:
alex: Heads-up — customer ACME reports invoice shows ~2x token usage for a 30m window yesterday. They say dashboard traffic and app logs only show one request per user. Can we triage?

maria: Thanks, forwarding to billing. Any request IDs or sample request bodies?

alex: Pasted the client's sample request id and headers: `req_id=acme-9f2b`, `Idempotency-Key: (none)`. They use a retry on timeout with exponential backoff.

billing-bot: Auto-note: checking ledger for req_id=acme-9f2b... found 2 ledger entries for different call_ids (call_101, call_102) totaling 16k tokens.

raj: If they don't send Idempotency-Key, gateway retries can create distinct server-side call_ids. Do we dedupe by Idempotency-Key only?

support-eng: Our metering pipeline dedupes by `idempotency_key` when provided; otherwise each accepted request creates a ledger row. Gateway should have dedup window for retransmits but last deploy changed how it surfaces upstream. I'm worried about an ingress retry loop.

maria: Do we have ingress-gw logs around their customer timeframe?

ingress-gw-bot: Found retries from source IP 35.198.12.7 between 2025-11-08T14:12:03Z and 2025-11-08T14:12:07Z. Retry policy: 3 attempts, timeout 2s. Upstream returned 200 on second attempt. Logged headers below:

```
GET /v1/generate
X-Request-ID: acme-9f2b
X-Forwarded-For: 35.198.12.7
Idempotency-Key: 
Call-ID: call_101
```

support-eng: Important: Call-ID differs on each retry (call_101 then call_102). Upstream 200 on second attempt, but both attempts were recorded to ledger because the gateway created a new call_id rather than reusing the initial call context. That explains double tokens.

alex: Any quick mitigation we can apply for the customer while we fix?

raj: We can run a one-off ledger dedupe job for that account: find rows with same X-Request-ID within a small time window and collapse duplicates to first-successful. But need approval from billing/legal. Also need to ensure we don't accidentally remove legitimate retries that increment tokens (e.g., streaming partials).

maria: Customer wants a credit if it's on us. I've asked legal. In parallel can we add temporary rule: when header X-Request-ID present, ignore ledger rows after the first SUCCESS within 10s from same customer?

support-eng: We can add a short lived patch to the metering pipeline to drop duplicates keyed by X-Request-ID + customer_id seen within 15s, but we must be careful with streaming endpoints where partial tokens are valid. For this workload the call pattern is single-shot generation.

ingress-gw-bot: Noting: recent gateway change (deploy 2025-11-01) removed reuse of upstream call context when client omitted Idempotency-Key. Patch: gw 2.7.3 created unique call_id per attempt. Reverting would reintroduce call reuse.

raj: Long term fix: enforce Idempotency-Key requirement (400 if missing) for non-streaming generate calls OR have gateway propagate initial call_id for retries and set a retry marker so ledger dedupe can operate.

alex: Filed internal bug: INF-5274 (gateway retry-call-id reassign). Adding prod logs and sample payloads.

maria: Action list: 1) billing/legal evaluate credit (I will follow up) 2) support-eng to run targeted ledger dedupe for account acme (awaiting ticket OK) 3) infra revert or hotfix gateway to preserve call_id on retries 4) product to evaluate Idempotency-Key enforcement.

support-eng: Quick repro steps for infra:
1) curl -v -H "X-Request-ID: acme-9f2b" -d '{"prompt":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate --connect-timeout 1 --max-time 3 
2) Observe gateway logs show two attempts, differing call_id headers 
3) Query ledger: `select * from ledger where x_request_id='acme-9f2b' order by created_at;`

raj: For metric reconciliation: run a tokens-aggregation grouped by call_id and by x_request_id, then compare to dashboard sums. This will surface other accounts affected.

maria: Thanks team. I'll wait on legal then authorize the dedupe. Customer pinged: "please expedite, it's a large hit to our monthly bill".

alex: Marking this high priority. I'll join infra call at 16:00 to discuss hotfix. :hourglass:
